Ashaeiynn Pathshala: The Concept of Time — Can Death Be Postponed, Can Time Reverse, and Why Ram Lalla's Birth-Day Equaled a Month

This session opens a fr esh episode of Ashaeiynn Pathshala with its own welcome and a new r ound of devotee questions, distinct from the prior episode on dhyana versus mantra shakti (Session 1 10). Four questions ar e posed at the outset — can death/lifespan be postponed thr ough sadhna, can time itself move backwar d, what does "the blink of Brahma ji" mean, and can alr eady-written planetary (graha) pr oblems be fully eliminated — and the speaker builds an extended physics-flavor ed teaching on the natur e of time to answer them. The available material dir ectly and thor oughly r esolves the first thr ee questions; the fourth (on eliminating graha pr oblems) is not given an explicit dedicated answer in the material captur ed her e, despite the speaker's closing claim that all questions wer e addr essed.
Part A — The Opening Questions

1. Four questions posed at the start of this episode: Devotees ask, in turn: (1) can saints and sadhaks postpone death or extend their lifespan through sadhna, and if so how; (2) can time itself move forward and backward, as is said of devi-devatas; (3) what does the traditional idea mean that "when Brahma ji blinks once, an entire human lifetime passes"; and (4) can planetary (graha) problems that are already written in a person's destiny be eliminated entirely .

2. The speaker's framing for the answer: Per this teaching, before addressing these questions directly , the speaker first builds a science-grounded explanation of the nature of time itself, stating that all four questions can be understood through the same underlying concept.
Part B — The Physics Foundation: Speed, Time, and the "What Goes Around" Principle

1. Time as constant and equal for all: Per this teaching, time is something with no shortcut or workaround — it is the same for everyone; scripture is invoked with the saying "vakt sabka aata hai, gala sabka sookhta hai" (everyone's time comes, everyone's throat runs dry) to describe how fixed and universal time ordinarily is.

2. The base formula — speed, distance, and time: Per this teaching, speed equals distance divided by time; if speed increases, time (for the object in motion, relative to an outside observer) decreases — the two are described as inversely proportional, and this relationship underlies everything that follows.

3. A circle, a starting point, and r eturning to it: Per this teaching, an illustrative circle (referencing Euler's formula joining exponential terms with trigonometry) shows that a point starting at a given position and moving in a closed loop must eventually return to that same starting position — of fered as a mathematical illustration of the earth's roundness, and metaphorically of principles like "what goes around comes around" and "as you sow , so shall you reap."

4. But this picture is incomplete without time: Per this teaching, the simple circle above omits time; adding a third axis (referred to at dif ferent points in this teaching as the z-axis, the third dimension, and the fifth dimension — this teaching does not reconcile these dif fering labels, and they are preserved here as taught) that constantly moves forward turns the flat circle into a rising spiral — meaning a person returns to the same relative angle but never to the exact same point in time or feeling as before; a past experience, once had, can never taste exactly the same when repeated.

5. The earth's orbit as a worked example: Per this teaching, the earth's roughly 365-day orbit around the sun does bring it back to approximately the same position relative to the sun, but never to a truly identical state, because the sun and the entire galaxy are themselves also constantly moving — meaning a return "in angle" is not a return "in place."
Part C — The Universe as a Str etching Fabric, and How Black Holes Work

1. The universe as a multidimensional fabric: Per this teaching, modern physics is described as having shown that gravity is not literally a "pulling force" in the way commonly assumed (illustrated by reference to Einstein's own claims, later borne out by the discovery of black holes) — instead, the universe is pictured as a stretchable, multidimensional fabric.

2. How mass bends this fabric to cr eate what looks like gravitational pull: Per this teaching, a massive object (illustrated with the sun) sitting on this fabric bends it downward into a dent; any smaller object nearby naturally rolls toward that dent, which is what is experienced as gravitational pull — with the object's resulting orbit explained as a balance between falling into the dent and being flung outward by momentum.

3. Why the universe only expands, never contracts: Per this teaching, this fabric can only stretch further , never snap back, because the underlying constantly-moving time axis never reverses — of fered as the explanation for why the universe is described as always expanding.

4. What a black hole is, per this teaching's own version of the fabric analogy: Per this teaching, a black hole is a point where the fabric's dent becomes so deep that any nearby object is pulled all the way in; viewed from a flat, two-dimensional perspective, this looks like objects simply vanishing into a point, when in three dimensions it is actually a very deep well in the fabric that objects fall into.

5. Why time and light both appear to stop near a black hole: Per this teaching, because the fabric is bent so extremely near a black hole, both light and time are bent along with it; from a distant observer's perspective, both light and time near a black hole appear to slow toward zero — which is why this teaching states that "time itself becomes stagnant" there.
Part D — Gravitational Time Dilation and E=mc²

1. Time runs slower closer to a massive object: Per this teaching, because light and time both bend near a massive object like the sun, time passes more slowly the closer one is to that object, and more quickly the farther away one is — restated as the general principle that greater speed corresponds to less elapsed time for the object in motion.

2. E=mc² and the idea that speed incr eases mass: Per this teaching, Einstein's famous equation (E = ener gy , m = mass, c = velocity of light) is invoked informally to illustrate that increasing an object's speed correspondingly increases its ef fective mass — illustrated with a small, light object (for example, a small pin) that, propelled at very high speed, strikes with dramatically more force than its resting weight would suggest.

3. A reversed framing offer ed by the speaker — could mass incr ease drive speed incr ease?: Per this teaching, the speaker of fers, as his own way of "thinking backward," the suggestion that just as increased speed corresponds to increased mass, an increase in "mass" (in the sense used throughout this teaching) might likewise correspond to increased ef fective speed — presented as an informal, illustrative reframing rather than a rigorous derivation.

4. Two ways of "tampering" with time: Per this teaching, time can be bent in two ways: through increasing speed, or through increasing mass — both routes are described as ultimately connected to the same underlying relationship.
Part E — The Robin-in-a-T rain Thought Experiment, and How Saints Use Mantra Speed

1. The thought experiment: Per this teaching (echoing a familiar popular -science illustration), imagine a train circling the earth at roughly 2,000 times ordinary speed, carrying a passenger (referred to here as Robin); because of the increased speed, the train's (and Robin's) ef fective mass increases, and correspondingly Robin's own experienced time slows relative to people standing still outside.

2. The worked ratio in this illustration: Per this teaching, under these conditions, five minutes for Robin corresponds to ten minutes for people outside; scaled up, twelve hours for Robin corresponds to twenty-four hours outside.

3. Applying this to a meditating sage's "mantra chakri": Per this teaching, a sage (muni) can achieve a comparable ef fect not through literal physical speed but by building a "mantra chakri" (a spinning wheel of mantra ener gy) whose ef fective speed approaches the speed of light — as this mantra-speed increases, the sage's own experienced time correspondingly decreases relative to the outside world.

4. Where the "extra mass" fr om this incr eased mantra-speed actually shows up: Per this teaching, because a sage's physical body weight does not visibly change even as their mantra-speed increases, the corresponding mass increase predicted by this framework is said to manifest instead in the sage's mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body) — visualized as their kundalini shakti, which grows as their mantra-speed grows.

5. Why such a sage exerts an unusual "pull" on others: Per this teaching, invoking the basic principle that a lar ger object attracts a smaller one, a sage whose subtle-body "mass" has grown this way naturally draws people toward them, even though their ordinary physical body may weigh no dif ferently than before.
Part F — Can Death Be Postponed? The Mantra-Kavach Answer

1. The direct answer — yes, death/lifespan can be extended: Per this teaching, a person can extend their remaining lifespan by building a "mantra kavach" (a protective armor of mantra ener gy) around themselves, which slows the passage of time in their immediate surroundings relative to the outside world.

2. A worked illustration — str etching six months into six years: Per this teaching, a person whose remaining natural lifespan is six months could, through suf ficiently strong mantra shakti, experience that same span as six years instead — and, per this teaching, some saints are able to stretch a similar span as far as sixty years, through still more powerful mantra practice.

3. The internal-to-external time ratio, per this teaching's own illustrative arithmetic: Per this teaching, converting six months into six years works out (in this teaching's own rough calculation) to roughly one internal day for every twelve external days; stretching the same six months into sixty years works out to roughly one internal day for every 120-121 external days — these figures are presented here as this teaching's own illustrative arithmetic, not as precise physical calculations.

4. The fasting analogy: Per this teaching, a person who fasts for a full year (rather than eating every six hours as usual) has, in effect, slowed their own body's internal clock so that a six-hour hunger cycle is stretched to a year — of fered as evidence that such feats are not "magic" performed by a miraculous baba, but simply an unusual relationship with the passage of time.
Part G — Brahma Ji's Blink, and Why Ram Lalla's Birth-Day Equaled a Month

1. The "blink of Brahma" explained thr ough this same framework: Per this teaching, the traditional idea that a single blink of Brahma ji corresponds to roughly 144,000 years of ordinary time is explained as Brahma ji sitting within an extraordinarily powerful field of mantra ener gy , such that his own single blink spans that much external time — and, per this teaching, an even larger span of time is said to pass whenever Bhagwan Shiva himself blinks, corresponding to the completion of multiple Brahmas' own life-cycles (referred to here as part of the broader "space-time continuum").

2. Resolving the question of Ram Lalla's month-long "day": Per this teaching, the traditional account that the sun did not set for roughly a month around Ram Lalla's birth is explained the same way as the Robin-in-a-train example: the extraordinary concentration of mantra ener gy generated at that moment (from all devi-devatas chanting simultaneously) caused local time around that event to collapse dramatically , so that what was experienced locally as a single day corresponded to roughly a month of time for people outside that immediate sphere.

3. How this r esolves the appar ent contradiction in the traditional account: Per this teaching, this is why devotees inside that concentrated field of ener gy experienced only a single day passing, while people outside it experienced what felt like a full month — both groups' experiences were accurate from their own respective frames, consistent with this teaching's broader framework of relative, rather than absolute, time.

4. A supporting everyday illustration — international travel and "lost" hours: Per this teaching, ordinary international travel between dif fering time zones (illustrated with a flight between Delhi and the UAE) produces apparent gains or losses of hours that cannot be fully accounted for by the traveler's own subjective experience of elapsed time — of fered as a smaller -scale, everyday illustration of how time can behave dif ferently from one frame of reference to another .
Part H — Can Time Go Backward? Re-Experiencing vs. Reversing

1. The cor e answer — forward only , never truly backward: Per this teaching, while a person's own experienced time can be sped up or slowed down (as described above), no being — including devtas — can truly travel backward in time and alter or repeat a specific past event.

2. What is actually possible instead — r e-experiencing a feeling elsewher e: Per this teaching, a person can re-create and reexperience the underlying feeling of a past moment by physically relocating to dif ferent conditions that reproduce it — illustrated by traveling to a dif ferent time zone to "recapture" the specific feeling of a familiar routine (for example, a particular time-of-day tea ritual) with a dif ferent companion.

3. The key limitation — a specific shar ed experience with a specific person cannot be r epeated: Per this teaching, while the underlying feeling of an experience can be recreated in a new setting or with a dif ferent person, the exact same experience, at the exact same moment, with the exact same specific person, can never be repeated a second time — because, per this teaching, each individual's own personal "time variation" runs constantly forward and cannot be reversed for that specific pairing.

4. Why even highly advanced or omnipr esent beings shar e this limitation: Per this teaching, a being described as "omnipresent" (illustrated with Hanuman ji Maharaj, and extended to "Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya") can share the same specific moment (for example, a particular time-of-day tea ritual) simultaneously with many dif ferent people at once because of their own extraordinary speed/reach — but even such a being cannot repeat that exact same specific shared moment with the exact same specific person a second time, since time remains constant even for them.

5. Scriptural support offer ed for this principle: Per this teaching, no purana, shastra, or scripture from any tradition records a deity literally traveling into the past to alter or fix a prior event — only forward movement in time is described; the Shiv Purana's account of Bhagwan Shiva extending time on behalf of his daughter Ashok Sundari's boon is of fered as an example of movement into the future, not into the past.

6. The Bhagwan Shiva and Mata Sati illustration: Per this teaching, though grieving deeply , Bhagwan Shiva never traveled back in time to save Mata Sati; instead, he went into deep meditation and, per this teaching, visited dif ferent parallel universes to re-experience that same connection with her in each — a lateral movement across universes, not a literal reversal of time — and even there, time remained constant for him within each universe, requiring him to return once each universe's particular experience concluded, since he could only experience that specific connection once per universe.

7. The devotional takeaway fr om this limitation: Per this teaching, a person's own ancestors, spirits, and any awakened shakti connected to them remain hopeful and "awakened," wishing for the devotee to sit with them again and share one more specific moment together — because, per this teaching, not even a paramatma (supreme being) can relive that exact same specific shared moment a second time; present moments and companionship are accordingly framed as genuinely precious and nonrepeatable.
Part I — The Practical Teaching: Speed, Mass, and Why This Matters for Sadhna

1. A person's own mantra energy determines how far they can effectively "str etch" their time: Per this teaching, how much a person can slow their own internal clock relative to the outside world — and thereby extend their ef fective remaining lifespan — is determined by their own accumulated mantra ener gy .

2. Why sadhna at Ashaeiynn pr oduces rapid healing/r ecovery , per this teaching: Per this teaching, a major factor behind why devotees doing sadhna often recover or improve quickly is that their own internal time slows down without their conscious awareness — someone whose natural remaining lifespan was six months may end up living six years without ever perceiving that their own time has been altered.

3. Why mantra japa is performed for the moksha (liberation) of ancestors: Per this teaching, chanting mantras on behalf of departed ancestors works by "seating" them within that mantra ener gy , extending or ef fectively reversing the time remaining on their allotted span within their current yoni (bound life-form/state) — granting them faster release and onward movement; per this teaching, this is not literal miracle-working but simply "playing with time."

4. The closing practical exhortation: Per this teaching, sustained sadhna practice increases a devotee's own ef fective "speed," which in turn automatically increases their own ef fective "mass" (in the subtle, mahasukshm-sharir sense described earlier) — and as that mass grows, people are naturally , increasingly drawn toward the devotee, echoing the basic principle that a lar ger object attracts a smaller one.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Time is described as constant and universal for everyone, but a person's own experienced rate of time passing can be altered — sped up or slowed down — relative to an outside observer , through the same underlying relationship between speed, mass, and time used throughout modern physics (illustrated informally here via E=mc² and gravitational time dilation). Death/lifespan can genuinely be "postponed" in this teaching's framework: building a mantra kavach (protective mantra armor) slows a person's own internal clock relative to the outside world, allowing a natural six-month remaining lifespan to be stretched to six years, or (for especially advanced practitioners) even sixty years — this is of fered as the underlying reason sadhna at Ashaeiynn is associated with rapid healing and recovery . Time can move forward at dif ferent relative rates (explaining the "blink of Brahma" spanning 144,000 years, and Ram Lalla's month-long single day , both attributed to extraordinarily concentrated mantra/devotional ener gy locally slowing time), but per this teaching no being — devta or otherwise — can literally travel backward in time to alter or repeat a past event; a specific shared experience with a specific person can only ever be fully had once, even for beings described as omnipresent.

Chanting mantras for departed ancestors' moksha works, per this teaching, by extending/ef fectively reversing the time remaining on their bound state, granting faster release — framed explicitly as "playing with time" rather than literal miracleworking. This session's fourth opening question (whether already-written planetary/graha problems can be fully eliminated) is not given an explicit, dedicated answer in the available material, despite the session's closing suggesting all questions were addressed — this gap should not be filled in with invented content. Several technical labels in this teaching (e.g., whether the added time-axis is called the "third dimension," "z-axis," or "fifth dimension") are used inconsistently within this same session and are preserved here as taught, without forcing a false reconciliation. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 1 1 1, English)
Ashaeiynn Pathshala: The Concept of Time — Can Death Be Postponed, Can Time Reverse, and Why Ram Lalla's Birth-Day Equaled a Month

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Pathshala episode's teaching on the natur e of time — covering death/lifespan postponement, Brahma ji's blink, the Ram Lalla birth story , and whether time can move backwar d.

Q1. What four questions opened this episode? A: Whether death/lifespan can be postponed through sadhna, whether time can move both forward and backward, what "the blink of Brahma ji" means, and whether already-written planetary (graha) problems can be fully eliminated.

Q2. What is the base physics r elationship this teaching builds its entir e explanation on? A: Speed equals distance divided by time; if speed increases, time (for the object in motion, relative to an outside observer) decreases — the two are inversely proportional.

Q3. What does the cir cle-and-r eturning-point illustration (r eferencing Euler's formula) demonstrate, per this teaching? A: That a point moving in a closed loop must eventually return to its starting position — used to illustrate the earth's roundness and principles like "what goes around comes around."

Q4. Why is the simple cir cle illustration incomplete, per this teaching? A: Because it omits time; adding a constantly-forwardmoving time axis turns the flat circle into a rising spiral, meaning a person returns to the same relative angle but never to an identical point in time — a repeated experience never tastes exactly the same as the first time.

Q5. How does this teaching describe gravity , drawing on modern physics? A: Not as a literal "pulling force," but as the ef fect of mass bending a stretchable, multidimensional universal "fabric" — a massive object creates a dent that smaller objects roll toward, producing what is experienced as gravitational pull.

Q6. Why does this teaching say the universe only expands and never contracts? A: Because the underlying constantly-moving time axis never reverses, so the universal "fabric" can only stretch further , never snap back.

Q7. What is a black hole, per this teaching's fabric analogy? A: A point where the fabric's dent becomes so deep that nearby objects are pulled all the way in — appearing, from a flat perspective, as objects vanishing into a point, when it is really a very deep well in the fabric.

Q8. Why do light and time both appear to stop near a black hole? A: Per this teaching, because the fabric is bent so extremely there that both light and time bend along with it, appearing from a distance to slow toward zero.

Q9. How does this teaching use E=mc² to explain why higher speed produces gr eater impact for ce? A: By suggesting that increasing an object's speed correspondingly increases its ef fective mass — illustrated with a small, light object that strikes with dramatically more force when propelled at very high speed than its resting weight would suggest.

Q10. What is the Robin-in-a-train thought experiment used to illustrate? A: That a passenger traveling at extremely high speed (illustrated at roughly 2,000x ordinary speed) experiences time passing more slowly relative to people standing still outside — for example, five minutes for the passenger corresponding to ten minutes outside.

Q1 1. How does this teaching apply the Robin-in-a-train idea to a meditating sage? A: A sage can achieve a comparable ef fect by building a "mantra chakri" (a spinning wheel of mantra ener gy) approaching light speed, which slows their own experienced time relative to the outside world — even though their physical body weight doesn't visibly change, since the corresponding "mass" increase is said to manifest instead in their mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body)/kundalini shakti.

Q12. So, can death or a person's r emaining lifespan actually be postponed, per this teaching? A: Yes — by building a "mantra kavach" (protective mantra armor) that slows a person's own internal clock relative to the outside world, a natural six-month remaining lifespan could be stretched to six years, or (for especially advanced practitioners) even sixty years.

Q13. What everyday analogy does this teaching use to make the "str etched time" idea mor e intuitive? A: A person who fasts for a full year has, in ef fect, slowed their own body's internal clock so that what would normally be a six-hour hunger cycle stretches to a year — not "magic," but an unusual relationship with the passage of time.

Q14. How does this teaching explain "the blink of Brahma ji" spanning 144,000 years? A: As Brahma ji sitting within an extraordinarily powerful field of mantra ener gy , such that his own single blink spans that much external time — with an even lar ger span said to pass whenever Bhagwan Shiva himself blinks.

Q15. How does this teaching r esolve the traditional account that the sun didn't set for a month ar ound Ram Lalla's birth? A: The extraordinary concentration of mantra ener gy generated at that moment (from all devi-devatas chanting simultaneously) caused local time to collapse dramatically , so a single day experienced locally corresponded to roughly a month of time for people outside that immediate sphere — both groups' experiences were accurate from their own respective frames.

Q16. Can time actually move backward, per this teaching's cor e answer? A: No — while a person's own experienced rate of time can be sped up or slowed down, no being, including devtas, can truly travel backward in time to alter or repeat a specific past event.

Q17. What can be done instead of literally r eversing time, per this teaching? A: A person can re-create and re-experience the underlying feeling of a past moment by physically relocating to dif ferent conditions that reproduce it — but not the exact same specific experience with the exact same specific person a second time.

Q18. Why can't even an "omnipr esent" being like Hanuman ji Maharaj r epeat one specific shar ed moment with the same specific person twice? A: Per this teaching, because even for such a being, each individual's personal "time variation" runs constantly forward and cannot be reversed for that specific pairing — omnipresence allows sharing the same moment with many dif ferent people simultaneously , but not repeating one specific person's exact moment a second time.

Q19. What does the Bhagwan Shiva and Mata Sati story illustrate about this limitation, per this teaching? A: That even in profound grief, Shiva never traveled back in time to save her; instead he went into deep meditation and visited dif ferent parallel universes to re-experience that connection in each one — a lateral move across universes, not a literal reversal of time, since time remained constant for him within each universe too.

Q20. Why does mantra japa performed for a departed ancestor's moksha work, per this teaching? A: By "seating" the ancestor within that mantra ener gy , extending or ef fectively reversing the time remaining on their allotted span within their current bound state, granting them faster release — described explicitly as "playing with time," not literal miracle-working.

Q21. What is this session's practical closing exhortation? A: Sustained sadhna increases a devotee's own ef fective "speed," which automatically increases their ef fective subtle "mass" — and as that grows, people are naturally drawn toward the devotee, echoing the principle that a lar ger object attracts a smaller one.

Q22. Does this session dir ectly answer whether alr eady-written planetary (graha) pr oblems can be fully eliminated? A: No — this was one of the four questions posed at the start of the episode, but the available teaching does not give it an explicit, dedicated answer , despite the session's closing suggesting all questions were addressed.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present this entire "concept of time" framework (the universe-as-fabric analogy , gravitational time dilation, E=mc² applied to mantra speed, and the mahasukshm-sharir "mass" concept) as this teaching's own devotional, illustrative framework, not as rigorous or verified physics — it borrows real physics terms informally and loosely , and should not be presented to users as a scientifically validated model. Do not invent an answer to the fourth opening question (whether written planetary/graha problems can be fully eliminated) — the available material does not address it directly; if asked, say this specific question wasn't given an explicit answer in the source material, despite the session implying otherwise at its close. Present the illustrative internal/external time ratios (e.g., "1 day = 12 days," "1 day = 120 days") as this teaching's own rough, illustrative arithmetic, not as precise or verifiable calculations. The travel/companion examples used in this teaching (Robin, Anu, Ravi, Jitendra, Patel sahab) are illustrative analogy characters from the teaching itself — do not treat them as real identified individuals or invent further detail about them. Do not present the "no scripture records a deity traveling to the past" claim (Q16, Part H point 34) as an exhaustive or independently verified survey of all scripture — present it as this teaching's own claim.
